detail: R-redesign-2-4-leaves-names-of-the-nine-re-f8a0: Redesign 2.4 leaves names of the nine retired agents in place (found 2026-10-26 by T-2026-10-26-003, deferred)

data.title: Redesign 2.4 leaves names of the nine retired agents in place (found 2026-10-26 by T-2026-10-26-003, deferred)
data.label: INFERENCE
data.what: INFERENCE — a reader of those texts looks for an agent that is no longer installed; on an upgraded home the agent sits in `backups/<date>/agents/`. No code path launches one: the `rr-*` skills name only the five.
data.likelihood: not prose only — `ai/policies/model-routing.md` still sends the session to `risk-tiers.json` for "which stages spawn an agent", and that file names `ai-tester`, `ai-planner`, `ai-security`, `ai-release` and `ai-expert` (template `risk-tiers.json:41-60, 87-88, 163-164, 386-400`): a session that follows it launches an agent this install no longer has, and the call fails. The `rr-*` skills do not read it. Same file, line 27: the `solo` direct-mode sentence is old tier vocabulary (STRONG review I1/L3 of T-2026-10-26-003).
data.fix: 2.6 rewrites `risk-tiers.*`, `test-run`, `quick` and the guard comment with the old subcommands; the seven role files go when `update.py` learns a retired-shared set (a project copy with no fallback is dropped, not refused) — its own task, behaviour 2; README and `docs/*` in 3.6.

detail: R-setup-py-reads-the-first-comment-of-a-sy-c19f: `setup.py` reads the first comment of a symlinked hook or script into toolbox.md (found 2026-10-26 by the T-2026-10-26-004 review, I1)

data.title: `setup.py` reads the first comment of a symlinked hook or script into toolbox.md (found 2026-10-26 by the T-2026-10-26-004 review, I1)
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: KNOWN FACT — a symlinked file under `.claude/hooks/` or `bin/` is opened and its first comment line is printed by `survey` and written into the committed `.ai/policies/toolbox.md`; a link pointing outside the repository would carry that line in. `.claude/hooks/*` also matches dotfiles. A dangling link is listed as UNKNOWN, no crash (reviewer-verified).
data.likelihood: needs a project tree that links a hook to a sensitive file whose first line is a comment; the threat model (`safety.md`) covers agent mistakes, not a hostile tree. Low.
data.fix: skip or label links whose target resolves outside the project root, and skip dotfiles under hooks — a separate task.

detail: R-risk-tiers-json-cannot-be-moved-to-weigh-2e14: risk-tiers.json cannot be moved to weight.json while the plugin still ships it (found 2026-10-26 by T-2026-10-25-008)

data.title: risk-tiers.json cannot be moved to weight.json while the plugin still ships it (found 2026-10-26 by T-2026-10-25-008)
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: KNOWN FACT — a draft 0007 with `MOVES = [(risk-tiers.json, weight.json)]` turned the invariant red ("a template is shipped at a path a migration moved away"), and its `delete?` of `risk-tiers.md` held every project at schema 6 until a human ran `--confirm-delete` (18 assertions in `test-project-update.sh` red). INFERENCE from `update.py:1233` and `:737`: after a confirmed deletion, the next run re-creates both files from the templates. Also KNOWN FACT: a fresh schema-6 scaffold already holds `weight.json` (2.1 shipped it), so a move collides there.
data.likelihood: certain for every project if 0007 moves or deletes before the templates are retired.
data.fix: 0007 as shipped converts the edits into `weight.json` and leaves `risk-tiers.*` alone; the move and the deletion belong with the template retirement (2.6), in a migration of their own — which renumbers 3.4b's `0008_renames.py`. Decide whether that is the plan, or whether the templates retire in 2.2a after all.

detail: R-a-shared-files-section-moved-to-the-end-e649: A Shared files section moved to the end of the router goes back on the next router change (found 2026-10-26 by T-2026-10-26-001, out of scope)

data.what: KNOWN FACT — the 2.3 router is the first template change since 0006. data.fix: strip the newline before the section in `split_shared_section()`, and keep the section at the end when the project had it there; then restore r7's byte-identical assertion.

detail: R-guard-port-five-differences-the-3-1-revi-b022: Guard port: five differences the 3.1 review found outside the boundary (found 2026-10-27 by the T-2026-10-26-006 review, I1-I5)

data.title: Guard port: five differences the 3.1 review found outside the boundary (found 2026-10-27 by the T-2026-10-26-006 review, I1-I5)
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: KNOWN FACT, each reproduced: (I1) a payload that starts with a UTF-8 BOM — jq parses it and can deny, the port allows; (I2) a NUL (`\u0000`) in a JSON string — bash printed "ignored null byte" on stderr, the port is silent, and two scope cases with a NUL in `notebook_path` differed; (I3) `HOME` unset — the shell guards died on `set -u` and allowed, the port decides and can deny; (I4) contrived patterns — an unterminated extglob `!(a|b)**(.`, the glibc-invalid `\<*`, `\>?`, `\b+`, `[^ab](^(a|))` against a newline; (I5) R15 says 3.10+, but `scripts/merge-codex-config.py:31` and `scripts/render-codex-agents.py:165` import `tomllib` (3.11+), so `tests/test_imports.py` fails on 3.10 — older than this task.
data.likelihood: I1-I4 need a payload or a config no runtime session produces; I1 is the only one that allows where the shell denied. I5 breaks the stated Python floor for two scripts.
data.fix: I1, strip one leading BOM before parsing; I5, a `tomllib` fallback or a 3.11 floor for those scripts (the CI matrix lands in 3.3a).
data.status_why: I1 BOM strip and I5 3.11 floor done; I2-I4 stay accepted as recorded (T-2026-10-30-0854-register-batch-2)

detail: R-guard-denies-a-compound-line-where-a-rea-57a9: Guard denies a compound line where a read-only one-liner on .ai/reports/ sits beside a shell $(...) (T-2026-10-28-2221)

data.title: Guard denies a compound line where a read-only one-liner on .ai/reports/ sits beside a shell $(...) (T-2026-10-28-2221)
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: KNOWN FACT — on 2026-10-29, in T-2026-10-28-2221, a command line holding a read-only python3 -I -c over events.jsonl and a shell $(grep ...) was refused as an interpreter one-liner that writes control files; T-2026-10-29-1655 hit the same deny recording this entry. INFERENCE (from the regexes, not run) — WRITE_WORD_RE counts $( as a write indicator and interpreter_text scans the whole line, so the unrelated shell part triggers it; -> matches WRITE_REDIR_RE (:168) only when a .ai/state/ or .ai/reports/ path follows the > (spaces after it allowed) with no quote, space, |, ;, &, < or > before the path; the refused command was not kept, so whether it did is UNKNOWN. A false deny on the safe side; splitting the command avoids it. Related to the entry "Interpreter tripwire residuals after M2/L4"; "Path guard after R22: what it no longer refuses, accepted" covers what the guard allows, not its false denies.
data.likelihood: occasional; one refused command, no wrong allow
data.fix: look for write indicators in the one-liner text only — behaviour 2 (allows what was denied), so full mode under hooks/CLAUDE.md; a task of its own, if done at all
data.status_why: human decision 2026-10-30: false deny on the safe side, split the command (T-2026-10-30-0854-register-batch-2)

detail: R-a-template-shipped-in-one-version-only-h-f066: A template shipped in one version only has no merge base, so any project edit to it is a conflict on every run (found 2026-10-26 by T-2026-10-25-008)

data.title: A template shipped in one version only has no merge base, so any project edit to it is a conflict on every run (found 2026-10-26 by T-2026-10-25-008)
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: KNOWN FACT — the fixture's hand-added `T0` example ("Fiscal printer bridge"), carried by 0007 into `weight.json` `examples.light`, is reported on every later run as `conflict .ai/policies/weight.json kept your value for: examples.light`. The project's value is kept and `--check` exits 0, but the word "conflict" sits beside a value the migration itself wrote. The same holds today for any hand edit to `weight.json`. Three exact-count assertions in `tests/test-project-update.sh` (`:95`, `:125`, `:130`) change from one hand-merge choice to two.
data.likelihood: every project with a hand-edited risk-tier example or path scope; noise, no data loss.
data.fix: either accept it and update the three counts in `tests/test-project-update.sh` (outside T-2026-10-25-008's files: SCOPE_CHANGE_REQUIRED), or let `three_way()` use the current template as the base when it is the only version ever shipped (the project was installed from it), which makes the carried values merge silently.
data.status_why: noise, no data loss; the conflict wording stays (human default 2026-10-30) (T-2026-10-30-0854-register-batch-2)
